text:
marta: @support team — customer ACME reported a sudden p99 spike and intermittent 504s for the /v2/generate route starting around 11:12 UTC. ticket: #12345. They say requests queue for ~10s before failing. Repro steps attached by customer below.

jia: looking. grabbing metrics now.

alex: seeing a correlated spike in request_queue_depth for the inference workers for that route. CPU on several pods is ~98% and kube HPA didn't scale further because pod concurrency limiter was triggered.

jia: key metrics I pulled: 
- api.v2.generate.p95 latency: 1.1s -> 2.3s (historic)
- api.v2.generate.p99 latency: 2.8s -> 12.4s (spike window)
- request_queue_depth (route=/v2/generate): from ~20 -> ~480
- worker_pod_cpu: many pods ~95-99%
- admission_rejects (concurrency limit): up from 0 -> ~320/min

alex: customer payloads are large (avg tokens ~1600) and they use streaming. Combined with long model kv cache times, each connection holds a worker slot longer than usual.

marta: customer provided curl repro: 
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v2/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-qa-xl","input":"<~1600 tokens of context>","stream":true}'
```

sam: running local repro now. also pulled worker logs for the window: 
```
[2026-03-14T11:12:34Z] INFO request_id=abc123 route=/v2/generate queued_for=11.4ms owner=customer-acme
[2026-03-14T11:12:45Z] WARN worker=inf-worker-7 cpu=98% kv_cache_hit=false processing_time=9.1s
[2026-03-14T11:12:54Z] ERROR request_id=abc127 upstream=timeout status=504
```

oncall-bot: incident created (INC-2026-0314-03) :rotating_light:

support-lead: escalation to eng-runtime and eng-sre. Customer is on Dedicated with burst policy; they want ETA and workaround. Please propose mitigations we can apply quickly.

jia: short-term mitigations we can do without infra changes: 
- ask customer to reduce streaming=true to false to avoid long-lived conn + try chunked response fallback
- temporarily lower max_concurrency_per_client for ACME route so they don't hog slots (rate-limit style)
- enable model fallback for this customer to redwood-qa-large (faster per-token) via routing rules
- increase admission queue size and temporary grace for this route (riskier)

alex: infra-side quick actions: 
- scale up Dedicated GPU pool by +2 nodes (if capacity available) — will require ops approval, ~5-10m to attach
- temporarily relax admission control threshold to allow autoscaler to create more pods (we saw HPA capped by concurrency limiter)

marta: customer prefers not to change prompts. ask them to accept fallback to slightly smaller model for next 30m while we stabilize?

support-lead: do it. @alex please schedule pool bump if capacity. @jia apply routing override to fallback model for customer-acme for 30m. i'll message customer with repro steps and suggested temporary change (disable streaming or allow fallback).

alex: starting pool bump request. pinging infra team. command I used to check pod concurrency limiter: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference get configmap admission-config -o yaml | sed -n '1,120p'
# look for concurrency_limit_per_route and queue_size settings
```

jia: applied routing override (temp): 
```json
{ "customer":"acme","route":"/v2/generate","override": {"model":"redwood-qa-large","ttl":"30m"} }
```
applied via admin console at 11:28 UTC.

sam: verified customer requests hit fallback model and p99 dropped to ~3.2s for a sample set. request_queue_depth stabilized from 480 -> ~45 within 4 minutes.

marta: updated customer: we applied a temporary model fallback and monitoring; also asked them to try disabling streaming. they confirmed partial improvement and asked for root cause.

alex: root cause analysis notes (preliminary): 
- combination of large context lengths + streaming kept worker slots occupied longer than expected (increasing effective concurrency)
- admission control thresholds were conservative and prevented rapid scaling under bursty concurrency from a single client
- autoscaler scaling delays + model processing time leads to transient queue buildup that hits p99 hard

jia: next steps (follow-ups): 
- ops: consider faster autoscale knobs for Dedicated pools or pre-warm nodes for large customers (action: alex)
- runtime: add per-customer adaptive concurrency limits and smoother admission fallback policy (action: eng-runtime)
- devex: add guidance in KB for customers using streaming with long contexts (action: support docs)
- run a postmortem and numeric threshold tuning for concurrency limits (action: eng-sre + runtime)

support-lead: I'll own customer comms + update ticket. Please add to postmortem board INC-2026-0314-03 and attach logs/graphs. Great triage and quick mitigation team. :thumbsup:

marta: marking resolved-for-now pending postmortem. thanks everyone.
